definitions.explanation: Describes someone who has recently entered or joined an organization, school, or group. Almost always used as a modifier before another noun.

examples.japanese: {新入|しんにゅう}{社員|しゃいん}の{研修|けんしゅう}が{始|はじ}まった。
examples.english: The training for new employees has started.

examples.japanese: {新入|しんにゅう}{生|せい}を{歓迎|かんげい}するパーティーを{開|ひら}いた。
examples.english: We held a party to welcome the new students.

examples.japanese: {今年|ことし}の{新入|しんにゅう}{部員|ぶいん}は{去年|きょねん}より{多|おお}く、{活気|かっき}がある。
examples.english: This year's new club members are more numerous than last year, and there's a lot of energy.

notes:
Used almost exclusively as a compound modifier:
・{新入|しんにゅう}{社員|しゃいん} (new employee)
・{新入|しんにゅう}{生|せい} (new student)
・{新入|しんにゅう}{部員|ぶいん} (new club member)

Contrast with {新人|しんじん}, which can stand alone as a noun meaning "newcomer" or "rookie".
